historic/u3e2/stamp-act-proof-sheet.jpg.description: Proof sheet of 26 one-penny embossed revenue stamps submitted to Commissioners of Stamps May 10, 1765. Shows the embossed mark colonists had to buy for newspapers, deeds, dice and every paper item, illustrating direct tax reaching into desk drawer.

historic/u3e2/pennsylvania-journal-skull.description: Skull and crossbones woodcut 'This is the place to affix the STAMP' from Pennsylvania Journal and Weekly Advertiser October 24 1765, publisher William Bradford parody of official stamp as death of press, used for tombstone edition Oct 31.

historic/u3e2/patrick-henry-burgesses.jp.description: Peter F. Rothermel 1851 painting Patrick Henry Before the Virginia House of Burgesses delivering 'If this be treason, make the most of it!' speech May 30 1765 against Stamp Act, source of Virginia Resolves claim only assembly can tax Virginians.

historic/u3e2/spinning-colonial-kitchen..description: Engraving 'Spinning in the colonial kitchen' 1885 after colonial practice, woman at spinning wheel. Illustrates Daughters of Liberty spinning bees, homespun cloth and nonimportation boycott that recruited British merchants to lobby for repeal.

historic/u3e2/james-otis-rights-colonies.description: Title page of James Otis pamphlet The Rights of the British Colonies Asserted and Proved, Boston 1764, bestseller arguing rights from God and nature, source of 'taxation without representation is tyranny' idea and actual representation doctrine vs virtual representation.

historic/u3e2/funeral-miss-ame-stamp-rep.description: British cartoon The Repeal, or the Funeral of Miss Ame-Stamp 1766. Grenville carries coffin marked 'Miss Ame-Stamp born 1765 died 1766' in Thames procession, warehouses empty from boycott. Visualizes boycott success, repeal March 1766 and context for linked Declaratory Act 'in all cases whatsoever'.
